fields.appearance: 1775, at Bajarāpura (Nadia, now Jessore) (the record's text)
fields.disappearance: Caitra śukla dvitīyā, 1844 (the record's text, after the Viśvakoṣa)
fields.place: Born at Bajarāpura (Nadia, now Jessore); studied at Kāśī; Calcutta (Sanskrit College); Śrīrāmapura (the Bengali press)
fields.disciples: Students: Īśvaracandra Vidyāsāgara, Tārāśaṅkara, Madanamohana, Śrīśacandra; the missionaries Carey and Marshman (Sanskrit and Bengali)
fields.works: Revised the Śrīrāmapura Bengali Rāmāyaṇa (Kṛttivāsa) and Mahābhārata (Kāśīrāma dāsa); Hari-bhakty-ātmikā (Bengali of Bilvamaṅgala's verses); Pārsī Abhidhāna; Ṣaḍ-ṛtu-varṇana
fields.notes: Son of Kevalarāma Tarkapañcānana, sabhā-paṇḍita of the Rājā of Nāṭor; studied at Kāśī; from 1805 worked under Carey; professor of literature at the Sanskrit College and teacher of Vidyāsāgara; revised the first printed Bengali Rāmāyaṇa and Mahābhārata. A Vārendra brāhmaṇa; no children of his own, adopted a son. Died 1844 (Viśvakoṣa VI, 660-661).

fields.name: Gorācāṅd dāsa Bābājī
fields.aka: Gorācānd Dāsa Bābājī, Goracand Dāsa Bābājī
fields.place: Rādhā-kuṇḍa (a mud kuṭīra on the north side)
fields.notes: Did bhajana at Rādhā-kuṇḍa early in the 20th century; knew the Caitanya-caritāmṛta by heart. Asked by Navadvīpa dāsa Bābājī why Kṛṣṇa is called «jñāna-vastu», the frail old bābā sang Kṛṣṇa's glories with a lion's energy for half an hour and fell unconscious. Told by Navadvīpa dāsa Bābājī Mahānta to Haridāsa dāsa.

fields.name: Vṛndāvana dāsa Bābājī (Varṣāṇā)
fields.notes: Lived at Varṣāṇā and walked every day to Vṛndāvana and back to visit the seven temples; never took prasāda anywhere. When he once did, at the Govinda temple, his chanting thumb froze: the money had come from a prostitute. Manohara dāsa Bābājī of Govinda-kuṇḍa (#1849) had him bathe in Śrī Kuṇḍa and go round Girirāja in wet clothes for three days, and his thumb was healed. (The guru field said only «Mahārāja».)
